source_text: Τί ἄν τις εἴποι περὶ τῶν ἐπῳδαῖς καὶ περιάπτοις κεχρημένων, καὶ νομίσματα χαλκᾶ Ἀλεξάνδρου τοῦ Μακεδόνος ταῖς κεφαλαῖς καὶ τοῖς ποσὶ περιδεσμούντων; Αὗται αἱ ἐλπίδες ἡμῶν, εἰπέ μοι, ἵνα μετὰ σταυρὸν καὶ θάνατον Δεσποτικὸν εἰς Ἕλληνος βασιλέως εἰκόνα τὰς ἐλπίδας τῆς σωτηρίας ἔχωμεν; Οὐκ οἶδας πόσα κατώρθωσεν ὁ σταυρός; τὸν θάνατον κατέλυσε, τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἔσβεσε, τὸν ᾅδην ἄχρηστον ἐποίησε, τοῦ διαβόλου τὴν δύναμιν ἐξέλυσε, καὶ εἰς σώματος ὑγίειαν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀξιόπιστος; τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀνέστησεν ἅπασαν, καὶ σὺ αὐτῷ οὐ θαῤῥεῖς; καὶ τίνος ἂν ἄξιος εἴης, εἰπέ μοι; Οὐ περίαπτα δὲ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπῳδὰς σαυτῷ περιάγεις, γραΐδια μεθύοντα καὶ παραπαίοντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν σου εἰσάγων· καὶ οὐκ αἰσχύνῃ οὐδὲ ἐρυθριᾷς μετὰ τοσαύτην φιλοσοφίαν πρὸς ταῦτα ἐπτοημένος; Καὶ τὸ χαλεπώτερον τῆς ἀπάτης· ὅταν γὰρ παραινῶμεν ταῦτα καὶ ἀπάγωμεν, δοκοῦντες ἀπολογεῖσθαί φασιν, ὅτι Χριστιανή ἐστιν ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ταῦτα ἐπᾴδουσα, καὶ οὐδὲν ἕτερον φθέγγεται, ἢ τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὄνομα. Διὰ τοῦτο μὲν οὖν αὐτὴν μάλιστα μισῶ καὶ ἀποστρέφομαι, ὅτι τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Θεοῦ πρὸς ὕβριν κατακέχρηται, ὅτι λέγουσα Χριστιανὴ εἶναι, τὰ τῶν Ἑλλήνων ἐπιδείκνυται. Καὶ γὰρ καὶ οἱ δαίμονες τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὄνομα ἐφθέγγοντο, ἀλλ' ἦσαν δαίμονες, καὶ οὕτως ἔλεγον πρὸς τὸν Χριστόν· Οἴδαμέν σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ Θεοῦ· καὶ ὅμως ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἀπήλασε. Διὰ δὴ ταῦτα παρακαλῶ τῆς ἀπάτης καθαρεύειν ταύτης, καὶ καθάπερ βακτηρίαν ἔχειν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο. Καὶ ὥσπερ χωρὶς ὑποδημάτων ἢ ἱματίων οὐκ ἂν ἕλοιτό τις ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν καθεῖναι· οὕτω χωρὶς τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου μηδέποτε εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐμβάλῃς, ἀλλ' ὅταν μέλλῃς ὑπερβαίνειν τὰ πρόθυρα τοῦ πυλῶνος, τοῦτο φθέγξαιτὸ ῥῆμα πρότερον· Ἀποτάσσομαί σοι, Σατανᾶ, καὶ τῇ πομπῇ σου καὶ τῇ λατρείᾳ σου, καὶ συντάσσομαί σοι, Χριστέ· καὶ μηδέποτε χωρὶς τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης ἐξέλθῃς· τοῦτό σοι βακτηρία ἔσται, τοῦτο ὅπλον, τοῦτο πύργος ἄμαχος. Καὶ μετὰ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου καὶ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου διατύπωσον· οὕτω γὰρ οὐ μόνον ἄνθρωπος ἀπαντῶν, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ αὐτὸς ὁ διάβολος βλάψαι τι δυνήσεται, μετὰ τούτων σε ὁρῶν τῶν ὅπλων πανταχοῦ φαινόμενον. Καὶ ταῦτα σαυτὸν ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη παίδευσον, ἵνα ὅταν τὴν σφραγῖδα λάβῃς, ἐμπαράσκευος ᾖς στρατιώτης, καὶ τὸ κατὰ τοῦ διαβόλου τρόπαιον στήσας, δέξῃ τὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανον· οὗ γένοιτο πάντας ἡμᾶς ἐπιτυχεῖν, χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, μεθ' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ ἡ δόξα ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Amulets, incantations, and the daily renunciation
orientation: Chrysostom is still warning the catechumens against pagan practices, now attacking amulets and incantations and giving them the baptismal renunciation as their daily weapon.
pass_a_gloss: What would anyone say about those who use incantations and amulets, and who bind bronze coins of Alexander of Macedon to their heads and their feet? Are these our hopes, tell me, so that after the cross and the death of the Master we hold the hopes of salvation in the image of a Greek king? Do you not know how many things the cross accomplished? It destroyed death, it quenched sin, it made Hades useless, it dissolved the power of the devil, and is it not trustworthy for the health of the body? It raised up the whole inhabited world, and you do not trust it? And of what would you be worthy, tell me? And not only amulets, but you also carry incantations around yourself, bringing drunken and raving old women into your house; and are you not ashamed nor do you blush, after so much philosophy, being terrified at these things? And the harder part of the deceit: for whenever we advise against these things and lead you away, thinking to defend themselves they say that the woman who chants these things is a Christian, and she utters nothing other than the name of God. For this reason therefore I hate her most of all and turn away from her, because she has misused the name of God for outrage, because while saying she is a Christian, she displays the things of the Greeks. For indeed the demons also uttered the name of God, but they were demons, and thus they said to Christ: We know who you are, the Holy One of God; and yet he rebuked them and drove them away. For these reasons therefore I urge you to keep pure from this deceit, and to have this word as a staff. And just as without sandals or clothing none of you would choose to go down into the marketplace, so without this word never go into the marketplace, but whenever you are about to cross the threshold of the gate, utter this word first: I renounce you, Satan, and your pageantry and your worship, and I enlist with you, Christ; and never go out without this utterance. This will be a staff for you, this a weapon, this an unconquerable tower. And with this word also trace the cross on your forehead; for thus not only a person meeting you, but not even the devil himself will be able to harm you at all, seeing you appearing everywhere with these weapons. And train yourself in these things from now on already, so that when you receive the seal, you may be a prepared soldier, and having set up the trophy against the devil, you may receive the crown of righteousness; which may it be granted that we all obtain, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father be the glory together with the Holy Spirit, unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.term: Ἀποτάσσομαί σοι, Σατανᾶ, καὶ τῇ πομπῇ σου καὶ τῇ λατρείᾳ σου, καὶ συντάσσομαί σοι, Χριστέ
choices.english: I renounce you, Satan, and your pageantry and your worship, and I enlist with you, Christ
choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary rendering for the renunciation formula and 'Satan's pageantry'; 'enlist with' renders συντάσσομαι as the military counterpart to renunciation, fitting the soldier imagery that follows.
rejected: I reject you, Satan, and your pomp and your service, and I join myself to you, Christ
I turn away from you, Satan, and your display and your worship, and I covenant with you, Christ

choices.why: Keeps the plural 'hopes' and the genitive 'of salvation' exactly, preserving the rhetorical force of the question.
Both participles are rendered as adjectives modifying 'old women', keeping the contemptuous diminutive γραΐδια as 'old women'.
rejected: drunken old hags who are out of their minds
old women who are drunk and delirious

choices.why: Keeps φιλοσοφία literally as 'philosophy', since Chrysostom uses it for the Christian way of life and the contrast is rhetorically pointed.

choices.term: τὸ κατὰ τοῦ διαβόλου τρόπαιον στήσας
choices.english: having set up the trophy against the devil
choices.why: Keeps the military metaphor of τρόπαιον as 'trophy', matching the soldier imagery of the passage.
rejected: having won the victory over the devil
having raised the standard against the devil

choices.why: συντάσσομαι is the military term for enlisting or being arrayed with someone; 'enlist with' preserves the soldier metaphor that Chrysostom develops immediately after.
rejected: I join myself to you, Christ

pass_b_english: What could anyone say about those who use incantations and amulets, and bind bronze coins of Alexander of Macedon around their heads and feet? Tell me, are these our hopes—that after the cross and the death of the Master, we place the hopes of salvation in the image of a Greek king? Do you not know how much the cross accomplished? It destroyed death, quenched sin, made hell useless, dissolved the devil's power, and raised up the whole world—and is it not worthy of trust for the health of the body? And do you not trust in it? Tell me, what would you deserve?

And you do not only carry amulets around with you, but also incantations, bringing drunken and raving old women into your house. And you are not ashamed, you do not blush, after so much philosophy, to be terrified by these things? And here is the more difficult part of the deceit: when we advise against these things and try to draw you away, they think they are defending themselves by saying, 'The woman who chants these things is a Christian, and she says nothing other than the name of God.' For this very reason, then, I hate and turn away from her most of all—because she has abused the name of God to insult Him, because while claiming to be a Christian, she displays the practices of the Greeks. For the demons also spoke the name of God, but they were demons, and they spoke to Christ in this way: 'We know who you are, the Holy One of God' (Mark 1:24). And yet he rebuked them and drove them away.

For these reasons, then, I urge you to keep yourselves pure from this deceit, and to hold this saying as a staff. And just as none of you would choose to go down into the marketplace without sandals or clothing, so never go into the marketplace without this saying. But when you are about to cross the threshold of the gate, say this saying first: 'I renounce you, Satan, and your pageantry and your worship, and I join myself to you, Christ.' And never go out without this utterance. This will be your staff, this your weapon, this your unassailable tower. And with this saying, trace the cross on your forehead. For in this way, not only will no human being who meets you be able to harm you, but not even the devil himself, when he sees you appearing everywhere with these weapons.

Train yourself in these things from now on, so that when you receive the seal, you may be a prepared soldier, and having set up the trophy against the devil, you may receive the crown of righteousness. May it be granted to all of us to obtain it, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father be glory, together with the Holy Spirit, to the ages of ages. Amen.

problems.quote: she has misused the name of God for insult
problems.source_quote: τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Θεοῦ πρὸς ὕβριν κατακέχρηται
problems.why: πρὸς ὕβριν means 'to insult/disgrace [God],' not 'for insult' as if gaining insult; it's abusive use of God's name.
problems.fix: she has abused the name of God to insult Him

problems.quote: and it is not trustworthy for the health of a body?
problems.source_quote: καὶ εἰς σώματος ὑγίειαν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀξιόπιστος;
problems.why: Rhetorical question expects positive: the cross IS worthy of trust for bodily healing. English reads as negative.
problems.fix: and is it not worthy of trust for the health of the body?
problems.ruling: Greek ἀξιόπιστος expects 'is it not trustworthy?' = 'it IS trustworthy'; English flips to negative.

problems.why: συντάσσομαι means 'I join ranks with/enlist under,' a military metaphor of joining Christ's army; 'enlist with you' is ambiguous (could mean recruiting Christ).
problems.ruling: συντάσσομαι means 'I join ranks with/enlist under'; 'enlist with you' is ambiguous, could mean recruiting Christ.

edits.old: she has misused the name of God for insult
edits.new: she has abused the name of God to insult Him

edits.old: and it is not trustworthy for the health of a body?
edits.new: and is it not worthy of trust for the health of the body?

fixed: Corrected 'for insult' to 'to insult Him' to reflect πρὸς ὕβριν as the purpose of the abuse.
Changed to a positive rhetorical question matching the source's expected affirmative answer.
Changed 'enlist with you' to 'enlist under you' to capture the military metaphor of συντάσσομαι.

problems.why: συντάσσομαι means 'I join ranks with/align myself with', not military 'enlist under'; it's covenant language, not subordination.
problems.fix: I join myself to you, Christ
problems.ruling: συντάσσομαι means 'I join ranks/align myself with', not 'enlist under'; 'enlist under' wrongly implies subordination.

edits.new: I join myself to you, Christ

fixed: Changed 'I enlist under you, Christ' to 'I join myself to you, Christ' because συντάσσομαι means 'to join oneself to/align oneself with', not military enlistment under a commander.

problems.quote: And you do not trust it?
problems.why: θαῤῥεῖς is 'you have confidence/trust'—but the Greek has 'σὺ αὐτῷ' (you in relation to it), and the previous clause asked about the cross's trustworthiness for bodily health. This follows as 'and you do not trust in it?'—correct.
problems.fix: and do you not trust in it?

problems.quote: And with this saying, trace the cross
problems.source_quote: Καὶ μετὰ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου καὶ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου διατύπωσον
problems.why: English omits 'ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου' (on your forehead)—'trace the cross' without 'on your forehead' loses the specific location.
problems.fix: And with this saying, trace the cross on your forehead
problems.ruling: ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου ('on your forehead') is omitted; specific location of tracing the cross is lost.
